statements.impact_statement: The issue is an RSA decryption timing side channel. The runtime GPG verifier is removed and a bounded executable-link audit found no remaining executable under /usr/bin, /usr/sbin, or /usr/share/cattle linked to libgcrypt.
The affected subordinate-ID allocation path is absent: login.defs, subuid, subgid, passwd, useradd, usermod, groupadd, newuidmap, and newgidmap are removed from the final runtime.
The upstream advisory lists affected Git release lines only through 2.48.1; the final runtime enforces Git 2.53.0 for Catalog HTTPS clone and fetch operations.

The final runtime installs the Ubuntu 26.04 security update 8.18.0-1ubuntu2.5 for curl and both shipped libcurl variants from the signed 2026-09-10 snapshot, and enforces the exact installed versions during image assembly and post-build validation.
The affected eu-strip utility is absent from the final runtime.
The affected eu-readelf utility is absent from the final runtime.
The final runtime removes both libexpat.so.1 and git-http-push, the sole executable that linked to Expat; Catalog requires only Git HTTPS clone, fetch, and checkout.
The vulnerable p11-kit RPC server executable is absent and the final runtime exposes no p11-kit RPC Unix socket.
GNU tar and the container source-build workflow are removed from the final runtime, so the vulnerable incremental restore path is absent.
GNU tar and the container source-build workflow are removed from the final runtime, so the vulnerable one-top-level extraction path is absent.
Ubuntu USN-8678-1 identifies 3.5.5-1ubuntu3.4 as the fixed Ubuntu 26.04 package version; the final runtime enforces that exact minimum.

The package database still describes the Ubuntu base layer, but the active OpenSSL CLI, libcrypto, libssl, engines, and legacy provider are replaced with verified upstream OpenSSL 3.5.8, the first 3.5 LTS release containing the fix, and their runtime paths and linkage are validated in the final image.
The package database describes the base layer, but the final runtime replaces libz.so.1 with verified upstream zlib 1.3.2 and validates the active mariadbd linkage.
The issue is in the privileged mount utility. mount and umount are removed from the final runtime; no SUID mount entry point remains.
The issue is in login -h processing. login is removed from the final runtime.
The vulnerable systemd-journald executable, service units, and sockets are removed from the final runtime.

The advisory is specific to diff3 line mapping. The final Server runtime removes /usr/bin/diff3 and validates its absence while retaining only the unaffected diffutils tools required by existing image checks.
The affected getfattr and setfattr command-line utilities are absent from the final runtime.
The final runtime replaces uniq with GNU coreutils 9.11 plus upstream fix commit d64e35a8a4c0e4608321433e0d84d917e4e36371 and runs a multibyte -w regression test during build and image validation.
The affected unexpand executable is removed from the final runtime.

GO-2026-5932 applies only to the unmaintained golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp packages. The committed source graph and govulncheck evidence contain no openpgp import or reachable symbol in authentication-service, compose-executor, or host-provisioner.

The final merged runtime removes libexpat.so.1, its implementation library and git-http-push. The image build and post-build validation check file absence and reject any libexpat entry in the dynamic linker cache. The remaining finding is package-database metadata, not an executable XML parser.

The affected CMS parser is gpgsm. Both gpgsm and gpgv are removed and their absence is validated in the final runtime; no GnuPG CMS decryption entry point is shipped.

After upgrading Host Provisioner and Compose Executor to x/crypto v0.56.0, only the checksum-pinned authentication-service binary retains module v0.55.0. Its exact v0.4.36 source and vendored dependency graph import md4/ripemd160 but no golang.org/x/crypto/ssh package. These two advisories require SSH channel dispatch, which is absent from that binary. This statement must not be reused for an SSH-bearing v0.55.0 binary.

The issue requires a caller to pass an attacker-controlled fopen mode containing an empty ,ccs= conversion specification. The Server runtime does not accept or construct fopen mode strings from user input; the image gate scans the exact Java, Go, shell and service entrypoint set and rejects any ,ccs= use. Ubuntu still lists the Resolute package status as needs evaluation, so this is an execution-path determination rather than a claim that package version 2.43-2ubuntu2.4 fixes the defect.

Ubuntu USN-8675-2 identifies 5.40.1-7ubuntu0.3 as the Ubuntu 26.04 fixed package revision for CVE-2026-12087. The final image installs and exact-verifies that revision for libperl5.40, perl, perl-base, and perl-modules-5.40 from the signed 2026-09-10 snapshot.
